summary: Kanban EV is a heavy Vital Lacerda worker-placement game about running an electric vehicle assembly line, juggling interlocking production stages, R&D, and logistics under constant time pressure. It's dense with interconnected subsystems and rewards careful sequencing across long sessions rather than quick, casual plays.
praised: deeply interlocking systems that feel like genuinely managing a factory
strong payoff when the engine clicks together
criticised: steep learning curve and heavy rules overhead
significant table presence and long playtime
theme feels more like a skin over the mechanisms to some players

interaction.kind: worker placement on shared action spaces, individual production boards
interaction.detail: Each player runs their own factory board and production chain independently, but actions are taken from a common set of worker placement spots with limited slots, so occupying one denies it to opponents for the round. There is no direct attack between players' factories, and any effect on others comes purely from racing for the same limited actions.

sources: VP from R&D track and patent progress
VP from assembly line efficiency bonuses
penalties for unmet demand or inefficiency
scoring.how_you_win: Players use action points across departments (R&D, assembly stations, sales, imports) to build an efficient EV production engine, fulfill contracts, and advance tech/patent tracks; after the fixed number of rounds, all engine, contract, and track VP are totaled and the highest score wins.
